title: Noetherian henselization of a Noetherian pair has the same completion
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a pair with $A$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $(A^h,I^h)$ be its henselization [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], with structure map $\eta:A\to A^h$. Thus $I^h=IA^h$. For the adic completions $A^\wedge=\varprojlim_n A/I^n$ and $(A^h)^\wedge=\varprojlim_n A^h/(I^h)^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], the canonical map $A\to A^h$ induces an isomorphism $\theta:A^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}(A^h)^\wedge$. Let $\gamma:A^h\to A^\wedge$ be the composite of the completion map $A^h\to(A^h)^\wedge$ with $\theta^{-1}$ (an $A$-algebra map). Moreover $A^h$ is Noetherian, $A\to A^h$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $\gamma:A^h\to A^\wedge$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: *Set-up.* By [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], $A^h=\varinjlim_{B\in\mathcal C}B$, where $\mathcal C$ is the (essentially small, filtered) category of ring maps $A\to B$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale and $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}B/IB$, with coprojections $\iota_B:B\to A^h$ ($\eta=\iota_A$), $I^h=IA^h$, the pair $(A^h,I^h)$ is henselian, and $A/I\to A^h/I^h$ is an isomorphism. Since $I^h$ is generated by $\eta(I)$, $(I^h)^n$ is generated by $\eta(I^n)$, i.e. $(I^h)^n=I^nA^h$, for all $n\ge1$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGV, proof: 'In the proof of Lemma 0A02 we have seen that $A^h$ is a filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras $B$ such that $A/I\to B/IB$ is an isomorphism'

proof.text: *$A\to A^h$ is flat and $\theta$ is an isomorphism.* By [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-flat-quotients], $\eta$ is flat and for every $n\ge1$ the map $\eta_n:A/I^n\to A^h/I^nA^h=A^h/(I^h)^n$ (step 1) is an isomorphism. The $\eta_n$ commute with the transition maps $A/I^{n+1}\to A/I^n$ and $A^h/(I^h)^{n+1}\to A^h/(I^h)^n$ (all are induced by $\eta$ and the identity), so they induce a ring map $\theta=\varprojlim_n\eta_n:A^\wedge\to(A^h)^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], which is the map induced by $A\to A^h$, and $\varprojlim_n\eta_n^{-1}$ is its inverse. Hence $\theta$ is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras, and $\gamma$ is an $A$-algebra map: $\gamma\circ\eta$ is the completion map $A\to A^\wedge$. (This step does not use that $A$ is Noetherian.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGV, proof: 'The first statement is an immediate consequence of Lemma 0AGU (lemma-henselization-flat, line 3105) and in fact holds without assuming $A$ is Noetherian'

proof.text: *Each $B\in\mathcal C$ is Noetherian.* Let $B$ be an object of $\mathcal C$. As $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale, it is locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism], so, applied to the affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the ring map $A\to B$ is of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], in particular $B\cong A[x_1,\dots,x_n]/\mathfrak a$ is of finite type over $A$. Since $A$ is Noetherian, $B$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGV, proof (the application of Algebra Lemma 00MB to $B$ needs $B$ Noetherian; left implicit in Stacks): Algebra Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); Morphisms Lemma Tag 01TQ

proof.text: *For each $B\in\mathcal C$, $B^\wedge\cong A^\wedge\cong(A^h)^\wedge$.* Let $B\in\mathcal C$ and $B^\wedge=\varprojlim_nB/I^nB$ its $IB$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] ($(IB)^n=I^nB$). $A\to B$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat] and $A/I\to B/IB$ is an isomorphism, so $\beta_n:A/I^n\to B/I^nB$ is an isomorphism for every $n\ge1$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers]; as in step 2 the $\beta_n$ induce an isomorphism $\varprojlim\beta_n:A^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}B^\wedge$. Let $\kappa_B:B^\wedge\to(A^h)^\wedge$ be the map induced by $\iota_B$ (levelwise $\bar\iota_{B,n}:B/I^nB\to A^h/I^nA^h$). Since $\iota_B$ is an $A$-algebra map, $\bar\iota_{B,n}\circ\beta_n=\eta_n$ (step 2), so $\kappa_B\circ\varprojlim\beta_n=\theta$; as $\theta$ and $\varprojlim\beta_n$ are isomorphisms, so is $\kappa_B$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGV, proof: 'For each such $A\to B$ the induced map $A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ is an isomorphism (see proof of Lemma 0AGU)'; the isomorphisms $A/I^n\to B/I^nB$: proof of Lemma Tag 0AGU (line 3105), via Algebra Lemma Tag 051H

proof.text: *$A^h\to(A^h)^\wedge$ is flat, hence $\gamma$ is flat.* Let $c:A^h\to(A^h)^\wedge$ be the completion map. For $B\in\mathcal C$ the composite $c\circ\iota_B:B\to(A^h)^\wedge$ equals $\kappa_B\circ c_B$, with $c_B:B\to B^\wedge$ the completion map (both are levelwise $b\mapsto\iota_B(b)\bmod I^nA^h$). $B$ is Noetherian (step 3), so $c_B$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat]; $\kappa_B$ is an isomorphism (step 4), so $c\circ\iota_B$ is flat (an isomorphism of $B$-algebras identifies the two module structures). Since $\mathcal C$ is filtered and $A^h=\varinjlim_{\mathcal C}B$ with coprojections $\iota_B$ (step 1), $c$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-rings-flat]. As $\theta^{-1}$ is a ring isomorphism, $\gamma=\theta^{-1}\circ c$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGV, proof: 'By Algebra, Lemma 00MB (lemma-completion-flat) the ring map $B\to A^\wedge=B^\wedge=(A^h)^\wedge$ is flat for each $B$. Thus $A^h\to A^\wedge=(A^h)^\wedge$ is flat by Algebra, Lemma 05UU (lemma-colimit-rings-flat)'

proof.text: *$\gamma$ is faithfully flat.* $(A^h,I^h)$ is henselian (step 1), so $I^h$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A^h$ [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion]. Let $\pi:A^\wedge\to A/I$ be the surjection with kernel $IA^\wedge$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] ($I$ is finitely generated, $A$ being Noetherian). Then $\pi\circ\gamma:A^h\to A/I$ is an $A$-algebra map (step 2), so it kills $I^h=IA^h$ and the induced map $A^h/I^h\to A/I$ is an $A$-algebra map; since $A\to A^h/I^h$ is surjective (it is an isomorphism, step 1), this induced map is the inverse of that isomorphism, so $\pi\circ\gamma$ is surjective with kernel exactly $I^h$. Let $\mathfrak m\subset A^h$ be a maximal ideal. Then $I^h\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\pi\gamma(\mathfrak m)$ is a proper (maximal) ideal of $A/I$; the ideal $\mathfrak mA^\wedge$ generated by $\gamma(\mathfrak m)$ maps under the surjective ring map $\pi$ into the ideal generated by $\bar{\mathfrak m}$, which is $\bar{\mathfrak m}\ne A/I$; hence $\mathfrak mA^\wedge\ne A^\wedge$. As $\gamma$ is flat (step 5), it is faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-faithfully-flat-maximal-ideals].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGV, proof: 'Since $I^h=IA^h$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A^h$ and since $A^h\to A^\wedge$ induces an isomorphism $A^h/I^h\to A/I$ we see that $A^h\to A^\wedge$ is faithfully flat by Algebra, Lemma 00HP (lemma-ff)'

proof.text: *$A^h$ is Noetherian.* $A^\wedge$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and $\gamma:A^h\to A^\wedge$ is faithfully flat (step 6), so $A^h$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-descent-noetherian]. Together with steps 2, 5 and 6 this proves every assertion.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGV, proof: 'By Algebra, Lemma 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian) the ring $A^\wedge$ is Noetherian. Hence we conclude that $A^h$ is Noetherian by Algebra, Lemma 033E (lemma-descent-Noetherian)'
